stem:
Chitra has the prime factorisation 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 and wants it in exponential form.

Which writing is correct?

options.text: Write 2 × 3 only, dropping the repeated factors instead of grouping them as exponents.
Write 2³ × 3², grouping three factors of 2 and two factors of 3.
Start from 2³ × 3² to invent the product, as if the exponential form produced the primes.
Divide the prime factors instead of multiplying them when writing the factorisation.

teacher.key_rationale: Repeated identical primes are grouped with exponents: 2³ × 3². Writing a bare 2 × 3 substitutes an incomplete product for the grouped form. Treating the exponential writing as what produces the primes reverses the direction. Dividing the primes confuses the operation.

mx_swap.reason: Real-world quantity-modeling CWO invents a different hinge; kept term_substitution, relationship_reversal, operation_confusion on grouping primes.
